Wakala

الوكالة

Also called: Wakalah; agency; Wakala-Ijara

Definition

Wakala is a Shariah-compliant agency contract in which one party, the principal, appoints another, the agent or wakil, to act on its behalf, usually for an agreed fee.

What it means

The agent acts within the mandate the principal gives it and is paid a fee agreed in advance. In an investment Wakala, the agent invests the principal’s funds in Shariah-compliant activities on the principal’s behalf.

In a Wakala Sukuk, an agent manages a pool of Shariah-compliant assets for the Sukuk holders. Wakala is also combined with Ijara, so that an agent procures an asset that is then leased.

How HAYKALAH uses it

Wakala is one of the contracts FINA. builds Sukuk on, and part of HAYKALAH’s Sukuk and fund templates. In the stadium precinct Sukuk framework it proposed in 2026, the completed stadium moves to an Ijara or a Wakala-Ijara; the framework is a proposal with no mandate.
